Verification page (lean-pkg)

How to read the comparison status on this page. This page is generated by lean-pkg 0.29.0 and is reproduced without change. For a result whose coverage row also names definition claims (47 of the 99 results in Lean), it says "its statement was not compared by a second checker", and its summary line counts only the other 52, because the comparator compares theorem statements and not definitions. Every theorem claim that a row names is compared: all 1553 theorems of comparator.json, in the comparator receipt of this release. The definitions are checked by Lean's kernel in the build; the comparator's restated theorems mention verbatim copies of them (ChallengeDefs/), which scripts/comparator/CheckFidelity.lean checks to be equal to the project's.

Verification

Verification at a glance

How to read this page. Lean has checked every step of the proofs listed here. It cannot check that a Lean statement says what the paper says: that comparison is yours. For each result below, read the paper's statement beside the Lean statement, and check that the hypotheses match.

With the manuscript's hypotheses, 59 labelled results are formalized in full, as are three displays and a remark (63 full rows), and 22 with a narrower conclusion; P:tube-rayleigh-transfer in full with one input supplied; steps, parts or narrower forms of 30 further results with inputs supplied; T:full-upper and T:intrinsic-second-moment are outside Lean.

  • Paper: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise: Second Moment and Exact Asymptotics, https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment at 4fa7e18a5b6d (file SHA-256 0c25620b49406456526beb8549b469062c0ab53084097a84d49eaacfa8a5e7a5).
  • Results listed: 118. In Lean with the paper's own hypotheses: 85; in Lean with extra hypotheses, named below: 31; not formalized: 2.
  • Verified: 115 of the 116 result(s) in Lean (for 51 of them a second checker also compared the statement); of the verified, 51 prove(s) a weaker statement than the paper's.

Hypotheses. The paper's own: the Lean statement assumes nothing the paper does not.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. The upper bracket uses the ceiling with K_0 R_sp (OccupationCeilingFinite, L8Completed); the comparison uses the exact ceiling at zeta = 1/2 over O itself (ClassOBridge, wave L14). v_Psi is the integral form; in the direct zero case Gamma = 0 the energies and the ceiling vanish (ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper), C_2 = 0 is not formalized.

Corollary C:static-interaction: Summable static interaction bounds

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves E:static-block-series in full; E:static-interaction, with the identification of the interaction map with sum sigma^n Y_n and the order bounds derived from the primitive inputs below; and E:independent-static-blocks from the per-block bound on adapted phases; the Gaussian parity, the first-variance bounds and that per-block bound are supplied.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: for the order bounds (E:all-static-phase-orders, n >= 1; circle bound from L:complex-phase): FockSandwich (E:fock-sandwich in operator form), CPInputs (E:cp-input with the inverse-root integral) and PropagatorBlock (the weighted block map as M_z(h)), with positive A_0 and self-adjoint B at every cutoff (supplied, with the named inputs, in StaticInteractionCompleted); FockSandwich, A_0 >= 0 and B = B^* are proved in wave L12 on the Fourier-side model (FockSandwichModel.static_interaction_model_paper), with the added restriction of an orthonormal real family psi_m of size m in L^2(mu_eps) for every Gaussian cutoff m (so mu != 0; the case mu = 0, where every positive-order term vanishes, lines 3126-3127, is not covered by that wrapper); the remaining inputs of P:static-phase-all-orders for the order bounds: entireness in the coupling, the coefficient identification, the band and the cutoff removals (see that row); the free estimate ||S_0(-+h)||_lambda <= sqrt(e), the group law S_0(-h) S_0(h) = 1, Z_0 = S_0(h)(f,g) and the norm comparisons ||Z_n||_lambda <= (lambda h)^(-1) ||Z_n||_(1/h), ||(f,g)||_(1/h) <= ||(f,g)||_lambda (lines 3273-3292); an abstract complete real inner product space stands for L^2(Omega; X_lambda); Gaussian symmetry, E<Y_r, Y_s>_lambda = 0 for r + s odd (line 3293); the first-variance bounds of P:static-phase-variance, E||Y_1||^2 <= e E:phase-born and |E<Y_0, Y_2>| <= N sqrt(e) E:phase-mean (lines 3275-3280); for E:independent-static-blocks, the per-block bound ||I_j y||^2 <= (1 + E(h_j, sigma_j, lambda)) ||y||^2 on phases adapted to the past (E:static-interaction with density and tensoring with the independent past, lines 3333-3337), adaptation being an abstract predicate preserved by each block, and ||S_0(h_j)||^2 <= e^(lambda h_j).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Wrappers static_interaction_completed_paper and independent_static_blocks_operator_paper state R_alpha, D_Gamma by E:phase-constants under the class of S:static-phase (only 0 < alpha < 2 is used; local finiteness is carried); the identification I = sum sigma^n Y_n and the per-block step are proved. E:static-block-series is proved with nothing supplied.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. CameronProducts.cameron_fractional_products and CameronFinal.fractional_products_all (wave L16, A2); TeX lines at edf7085f. Smooth Littlewood-Paley bands replace the sharp dyadic bands, so C_s (CameronProducts.Cs) is 2^(alpha/4) times the sharp-band value; it depends on (alpha, s) only. Gamma = 0 included. Pairings and E:cameron-fractional-absolute for physical functions (IsPhysRep).

Lemma L:complex-phase: A complex phase bound

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, with the lemma's hypotheses, the numerical-range and scalar steps on W(L) with nothing supplied, and, with the inputs below, the bounds 3, 6(1+lambda h), 6 (times e^(lambda h)) for C_h(L), F_h(L), H_h(L), the root comparisons 7/6, 6/5 and the bound 100 e^(2 lambda h) for the weighted block map; its identification with M_z(h) is not formalized.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:cp-input (Crouzeix-Palencia, main TeX lines 2739-2748, imported in the TeX) for C_h, F_h, H_h at L = A_0 - zB with its holomorphy precondition: operators of norm at most (1+sqrt 2) M whenever the scalar function is bounded by M on W(L); the inverse-root integral representation of lines 2801-2826 for L^* = A_0 - conj(z)B (bounded holomorphic calculus): Q' - 1 = pi^(-1) int_0^inf J(t) dt with J strongly measurable and ||J(t)|| <= (|z| d/(1-delta_a)) t^(-1/2) kappa^(a-3).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Not formalized: the phase propagator M_z(h) and its identification with the weighted block map (lines 2920-2931, 2948-2951). A_rho^(-1/2) is the inverse of the continuous-functional-calculus square root, proved invertible for rho > 0. The self-adjointness of B is carried but unused.

Note. Under H:homog alone in DampedSmoothing.damped_homogeneous_norms_whole_paper (wave L12; d = 3 Green measure via toSphere, M1). Spatial smoothing gives e^(-eps|xi|^2/2) mu, the unique tempered spectral measure of p_eps * Gamma, taken as the measure with density gamma_eps (M3). Green smoothing p*G gives the multiplier e^(-v|xi|^2), identified with N_{2,m,S} in d = 1, 2, 3.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Wrappers FiniteWordCutoff.finite_word_cutoff_paper (any finite word with r_i <= N_i, J_i = sum_j M_(g_ij) tensor K_ij, the cutoff on the total degree of each color) and finite_word_cutoff_integral (finite sums and integrals of words, coordinatewise); nothing supplied; model choice M2 (Hermite coefficients, integrals coordinatewise). One-mode case: HermiteWordFock.

Lemma L:fixed-split: A fixed degree-split estimate

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves E:fixed-split-bound with C_split = 100^8 e^8 max(1, 12 delta^(-2)) for any delta > 0, on a finite Fock model of the cutoff Gaussian space with abstract spatial operators, for coefficients of an evolution that is not constructed; the segment bound, the Dyson cube identity, the invariance of the cross subspaces, entire coefficients and E:interval-column are supplied.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:interval-column (main TeX lines 3388-3391) for the modes of each color at every rho > 0, as the named input FockColumn of FockForm; the segment bound of L:interval-complex for the background propagators, ||P_z(t,s)|| <= 100 e^(2 Lambda (t-s)) on every interval free of background endpoints, as applied in E:split-segment-product (lines 3791-3801; SegmentBound); its operator theory is not formalized; E:interval-cross-cube (lines 3937-3960) on the torus of the background radii, with the integrability of the word on each simplex (DysonCrossCube); variation of constants is not formalized; the invariance of every cross subspace Z_S under the background propagator (lines 3855-3859; BackgroundPreserves) and the absolute convergence of the ordinary coefficients on every polydisc (lines 3729-3733; EntireCoefficients); the cutoff evolution, its propagators and the coefficients U_r v are not constructed.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Under H:homog (R = R_alpha carried, unused; alpha < 2), sigma_i > 0, any delta > 0 (not delta_(alpha/2)). S_rho = A_rho^(-1/2) symmetric, norm <= 1/rho, spectral comparison; M_e symmetric; S_b symmetric idempotent commuting with S_rho: assumed TeX properties. hQ is no hypothesis here: the P:interval-coefficients assembly adds it in FixedSplit (accepted 2026-11-12); FiniteWordCutoff removes it.

Lemma L:fock-form: Gaussian cutoff form bound

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, E:fock-sandwich, in coefficient form and as an operator-norm bound with A_0 >= 0 and B bounded self-adjoint on the cutoff Hilbert space, uniformly in eps, m and the band, for finitely many real modes, Hermite degree at most N in the m multiplied coordinates, on a Fourier-side model not identified with the physical-space operators.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

    (hPC : PhaseCovariance alpha Γ μ)
    (hRdef : R = alpha * π * (μ (Metric.ball 0 1)).toReal / (2 * Real.sin (π * alpha / 2)))
    (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : Fin m → Lp ℂ 2 (nuEps μ ε)) (hψ : Orthonormal ℂ ψ)
    (hreal : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ξ ∂(nuEps μ ε), ψ i (-ξ) = conj (ψ i ξ)) (N : ℕ) (b : ℝ) :
    let A0 := opA0 (d := 3) (m := m) (N := N) b
    let B := fieldB (N := N) b (nuEps_finite hPC.μ_tempered hε) ψ hψ
    let P := toH (m := m) (N := N) (diagOp (bandProj (d := 3) b))

      (∀ ρ (hρ : 0 < ρ), invSqrtShift A0 ρ * P = toH (diagOp (sqrtResolvent ρ hρ)) * P) ∧
      FockSandwich A0 B (fockD N R) (alpha / 2)

theorem _root_.StratonovichHamSecondMomentLeanAudit.StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FockColumnBound.fock_form_paper_completed {alpha R ε ρ b : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd 3)}
    (hPC : PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance alpha Γ μ)
    (hRdef : R = alpha * π * (μ (Metric.ball 0 1)).toReal / (2 * Real.sin (π * alpha / 2)))
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hρ : 0 < ρ) {m : ℕ} (ψ : Fin m → Lp ℂ 2 (nuEps μ ε))
    (hψ : Orthonormal ℂ ψ) (hreal : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ξ ∂(nuEps μ ε), ψ i (-ξ) = conj (ψ i ξ))
    (N : ℕ) {v : (Fin m → ℕ) → Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (Rd 3))} (hv : Supp N v) :
    let H := fun i => sqrtResolvent ρ hρ ∘L
      modes (nuEps_finite hPC.μ_tempered hε) ψ hψ i ∘L sqrtResolvent ρ hρ
    let P := bandProj (d := 3) b
    ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v k‖ ^ 2 ≤
        (StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD N R * ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2)) ^ 2 * ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖v k‖ ^ 2 ∧
      Integrable (fun x => ‖iota N (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v) x‖ ^ 2)
        (GaussianIBP.stdPi m) ∧
      ∫ x, ‖iota N (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v) x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m ≤
        (StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD N R * ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2)) ^ 2 *
          ∫ x, ‖iota N v x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m ∧
      ∀ w : (Fin m → ℕ) → Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure (Rd 3)), Supp N w →
        ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v k) (w k) =
          ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (v k) (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) w k)

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:cp-input (Crouzeix-Palencia, main TeX lines 2739-2748) for C_h, F_h, H_h at L = A_0 - V with weight Lambda: operators of norm at most (1+sqrt 2) M whenever the scalar function is bounded by M on W(L); the inverse-root integral representation of lines 3511-3526 for L^* = A_0 - V^*: Q' - 1 = pi^(-1) int_0^inf J(t) dt with J strongly measurable and ||J(t)|| <= (D/(1-delta_a)) t^(-1/2) kappa^(a-3).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Proved for E:interval-metric: the multiplier form of the weight change, the jump ratio, the product over jumps with pairwise disjoint ending sets, and the telescoping of the conversion factors along a monotone partition (wave L10). Their composition with the segment propagators is proved only inside L:fixed-split, with the segment bound supplied. The self-adjointness of V is not needed.

Lemma L:interval-contractions: Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, E:interval-column, its band-compressed form, the phase-insertion bound sqrt(R_alpha) rho^((alpha-2)/2), the sandwich bound R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) with self-adjointness and E:interval-fock, for finitely many real modes, on a Fourier-side model not identified with the physical-space operators, without tensoring by another Hilbert factor.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Lemma L:spatial-static-controls: Smooth temporal controls

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check of this result passed (the build, and the statement comparison).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: lambda is the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, and I_Psi, v_Psi are given by their integral formulas (identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 is not formalized); E:spatial-static-score is proved both in the form that every number below the bound is exceeded by some admissible score and in its supremum form, with nothing supplied.

Lemma L:symplectic-free: Free wave form and compact Young baseline

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves both compact-baseline displays on an abstract nonzero Hilbert space with a supplied free group, isometric velocity reversal and weakly vanishing translations, for a Young evolution given only by convergence of its left Young sums; it proves W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp per frequency and the force skewness for the L^2 pairing. J_E and the preservation of omega on E are not formalized.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: the free wave group on E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2) with its group law, the isometric velocity reversal with S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R, and the spatial translations, isometric, commuting with S_E(h) and weakly null as |y| -> infinity (integrated_symplectic_phase.tex lines 121-145); E is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert space; P:constant-young-linear on L(E) (integrated_symplectic_phase.tex lines 105-112): the left Young sums of X over partitions of [s,t] converge in operator norm to U_X(t,s) - I; supplied in the weaker form of convergence along some nontrivial filter of finite node lists in [s,t] (no ordering, endpoint or mesh condition).

Lemma L:uniform-mean-cutoff: Uniform cutoff and physical mean

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, for every real sigma and R >= 1, a bounded operator on H^sigma agreeing with multiplication by eta_R on real tests, of norm at most M_sigma (uniqueness not stated; tests are proved dense for sigma <= 1, covering the case sigma = 1/2 used), the embedding H^s -> H^t of norm at most one for t <= s, and E:uniform-spatial-mean for every T with the row at all states.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

theorem _root_.StratonovichHamSecondMomentLeanAudit.StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_constructed_paper {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (x : Rd d) (W : Pt d T → Ω → ℝ) (K : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ)
    (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) (hVfin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K p p))
    (hcell : MeanSquareCellContinuous K) :
    let ν : ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → Pt d T) := fun n => chainMeasure d n T hT.le x
    (∀ n, Integrable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW z) (ν n)) ∧
      ((chainIntegral ν hW 0 : Ω → ℝ) =ᵐ[P] fun _ => 1) ∧
      (∀ n, ‖chainIntegral ν hW n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ((2 * n - 1).doubleFactorial) *
        (⨆ p, K p p) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial)) ∧
      (∀ m n, ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P =
        ∑ D ∈ pairings (univ : Finset (Fin (m + n))), pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
      (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)),
        Integrable (fun q : (Fin m → Pt d T) × (Fin n → Pt d T) =>
          pairWeight (fun a b => K (Fin.append q.1 q.2 a) (Fin.append q.1 q.2 b)) univ D)
          ((ν m).prod (ν n))) ∧
      (∀ m n, Odd (m + n) → ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P = 0) ∧
      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) →
        (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)), 0 ≤ pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
        ∀ m n, 0 ≤ ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P) ∧
      (∀ r : ℝ, Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • chainIntegral ν hW n‖) ∧
      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) → ∀ r : ℝ,
        UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput P (fun n => chainIntegral ν hW n) r)

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: CutoffCompact d: compactness sentence of P:cutoff-singular-values (compact_gaussian 469-472, Step 1 487-519, at edf7085f): for real compact smooth chi, real sigma, gamma > 0, a compact bounded H^(sigma+gamma) -> H^sigma agreeing with multiplication by chi on real tests exists, and any two bounded operators agreeing with it on real tests are equal; TRUE; no singular-value rate or Schatten class.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. CameronSpatial.spatial_mean_map, cameron_spatial_map (wave L16, B2); CameronFinal.spatial_mean_map_paper (nothing supplied), cameron_spatial_map_paper (CutoffCompact); TeX at edf7085f. Constructs L15's CameronSpatialMap, compact by CutoffCompact. Also credited: the CameronSpatialMap structure and L15's PositiveRawMean.T_eq_BE, T_kBochner_eq (a CameronSpatialMap parameter).

Proposition P:cameron-temporal-map: The compact temporal mean, without trace class

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, with nothing supplied, for 2 < r < 2/a: K is bounded, positive, strictly positive, injective and compact; a positive square root K^(1/2) is compact; iota : H_t -> L^2(I) is onto and isometric with iota [f] = K^(1/2) f; C_t = K^(1/2) iota is compact into L^r(I), C_t f = K f on tests. Not trace class and not Hilbert-Schmidt are stated as cell-sum identities (decision 7).

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:interval-energy-splits combined with the reflection parity (lines 4147-4157), the coefficient as the sum over degree vectors kappa (sum kappa_i = k) and splits r_i + q_i = 2 kappa_i of Q_(r,q); the inputs of L:fixed-split for every split (E:interval-column, the segment bound of L:interval-complex, E:interval-cross-cube, the invariance of the cross subspaces and entire coefficients; see the row of L:fixed-split), with the interval endpoints (a_i, b_i) in [0, T], b_i - a_i <= h_i, and any delta > 0 in C_split = 100^8 e^8 max(1, 12 delta^(-2)); for E:interval-phase-bound, the power-series identity at s = 1 (lines 4092-4136, 4248-4255), the vanishing of odd coefficients (lines 4152-4154) and the zero-order bound e ||v||^2 (lines 4260-4261); the Duhamel word expansion of the ordinary coefficients (lines 4092-4097, 4166-4170; DuhamelWords): U_r v and the cutoff coefficient c_r are the same finite sum of integrals of words with r_i insertions of color i, uncut and cut; the evolutions are not constructed; from DuhamelWords Lean proves |Q_(r,q)| <= |<c_r, c_q>|, which the earlier step row assumed as the added hypothesis hQ (accepted by Le for now on 2026-11-12); Q_(r,q) is the real part of <U_r v, U_q v>_(1/T); the reduction to sigma_i > 0 (zero noise and sign change, lines 4079-4085); not formalized.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Wrappers under H:homog with R_alpha of line 3370; constant 12 max(c,0) max(1,L)^beta C_split C_inv. L:inventory-product is discharged in IntervalScalarCompleted, L:fixed-split in FixedSplit; the hQ that Le accepted on 2026-11-12 is removed in FiniteWordCutoff.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words (DuhamelWords instead). Zero noise and the sign reduction not formalized.

The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: the covariance matrix A of the masked evaluations W(zeta_R F_1), ..., W(zeta_R F_m) and the auxiliary Gram matrix B of N_R (lines 262-264, 320-321), which need the noise W and the completion of the test space (D1); A <= B in positive semidefinite order, from E W(zeta_R F)^2 <= N_R(F)^2 (P:masked-auxiliary-norm with H = H_a^C and E:masked-actual-noise-norm, lines 304-305, 321-322); the joint centered Gaussian law of the masked evaluations, so that their law is N(0,A) (lines 260-262, 308-311).

Note. The Lean theorems are a standalone finite result with no hypothesis standing for the inputs; their link to the noise is the inputs listed. Route: N(0,B) = N(0,A) * N(0,B-A) by characteristic functions replaces the product-space coupling, then Jensen for y -> N(x+y)^p.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:static-ratio-input (Chen-Hu static law, lines 8256-8264): 0 < L_0 and T^(-kappa_st) log E U(T,x)^p -> p^(kappa_st) L_0 for p = 1, 2 (fields L0_pos, static_law); E:full-moment-positive-series of L:full-moment-coefficient-holder with c_(p,0)(a) = 1 (E:full-moment-coefficients), nonnegative coefficients, summable for t > 0, 0 <= a < a_max (field series); E:full-moment-coefficient-holder of L:full-moment-coefficient-holder (field holder); E:static-minorant-rate of P:static-minorant-lower, as: every y < p^(kappa_st) L_0 is eventually below T^(-kappa(a)) log E u^(a)(T,x)^p, 0 < a < a_max (field minorant); E:full-upper-bound of T:full-upper at temporal exponent a: E u^(a)(T,x)^2 <= e (T+2)^d exp(C T^(kappa(a))) for T >= 1, one finite C (field full_upper); Cauchy-Schwarz (E u^(a)(T,x))^2 <= E u^(a)(T,x)^2 (field cauchy_schwarz; proof line 8795).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Under H:homog and Gamma != 0 (carried; only alpha < 2 is used). Moments are abstract functions mom p a T at a fixed x; rates are extended reals and the inequality is stated for their toReal values, which are the rates since finiteness is proved. log Lambda-bar_p is convex on [0, a_max).

Proposition P:riesz-small: Riesz finite coefficients

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves, with nothing supplied, E:riesz-two and the total E X_1^2 + 2 E X_2 for the chaos terms of every source field, E:riesz-two and A_1 = J_(1,1) + 2 J_(2,0) for the M4 diagrams, and E:riesz-four with finiteness for all splits and pairings (density diagrams, equal to the limit diagrams); the multiplicities of E:total-four are not formalized.

Hypotheses. The paper's own: the Lean statement assumes nothing the paper does not.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Under H:homog and Gamma != 0, nothing supplied (ClassOH1.spatial_four_linear_whole_paper, wave L14); H^1 is the weak-gradient graph H1R d (M6), whose topology is Mathlib's H^1 topology; joint continuity of C_4 on (H^1)^4 in the product topology. Density of C_c^inf in H^1 proved in H1Density. B_Gamma is OccupationKernelRow.pairing.

Proposition P:spatial-smooth-ratio: The finite smooth spatial ratio

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check of this result passed (the build, and the statement comparison).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: E:spatial-smooth-score is proved, with nothing supplied, both in the form that every y below the bound is exceeded by some I_Psi - v_Psi/2 and as a bound on the supremum, with lambda the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and v_Psi given by its integral formula (identification with sqrt(-E_s) and E W(Psi)^2 is not formalized). R_0 < inf is proved by L:spatial-fourier-bound.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's own: the Lean statement assumes nothing the paper does not.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Under H:homog and Gamma != 0 with nothing supplied, R_0 is positive and finite by L:spatial-fourier-bound, the manuscript's route since revision a284420, so R_0 < inf does not depend on T:full-upper; B_Gamma is spatialPair, equal to the extended pairing (pairing_eq_spatialPair).

Proposition P:static-phase-all-orders: All regularized static phase orders

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves the Cauchy coefficient estimate, the arithmetic at lambda = n/h and the series bound of the proof, and from them both displays for abstract Banach-space quantities, with the circle bound (or the inputs of L:complex-phase and E:fock-sandwich), entireness, the coefficient identification, the norm comparisons, the cutoff removals and the free bound supplied; phases are not constructed.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: the bound 100 e^(2 lambda h) for the phase propagator on the coupling disc of radius delta_(alpha/2) lambda^(2-alpha/2)/d', for every d' >= d_n, d' > 0 (lines 3129-3132), supplied in StaticPhaseCauchy; in static_phase_all_orders_cp the circle bound is derived from L:complex-phase and three named inputs: FockSandwich (E:fock-sandwich in operator form), CPInputs (E:cp-input, inverse-root integral) and PropagatorBlock, with positive A_0 and self-adjoint B at every cutoff (supplied, with the named inputs); in FockSandwichModel.static_phase_all_orders_model (wave L12) FockSandwich, A_0 >= 0 and B = B^* are proved on the Fourier-side model, not identified with physical space; the added restriction of static_phase_all_orders_model: an orthonormal real family psi_m of size m in L^2(mu_eps) for every Gaussian cutoff m (so mu != 0; the case mu = 0, where every positive-order term vanishes, lines 3126-3127, is not covered by that wrapper); the phase entries are entire in the coupling (lines 3134-3135); the identification of the n-th coefficient, applied to S_b(f,g) times the vacuum, with the cutoff n-th Duhamel phase via L:finite-word-cutoff (lines 3143-3148), with ||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h) (line 3154); L:finite-word-cutoff is proved with several coordinates per color (FiniteWordCutoff), but the identification of the phase coefficients is not formalized; ||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <= ||(f,g)||_(1/h) (line 3155); the removal of the band and Gaussian cutoffs, as convergence of the norms (lines 3168-3192); the free bound ||Z_0(h)||_(1/h) <= sqrt(e) ||(f,g)||_(1/h) (line 3207).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Abstract complex and real Banach spaces stand for L^2(Omega; X_lambda); the wrappers state R_alpha by E:phase-constants and A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2) with delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)} proved positive; the Gaussian-polynomial structure and the uniformity in eps are those of the inputs.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: TubeTail: P(d_delta(X) > r) <= e^(-r^2/(2 delta)) for r >= 0 (second part of E:tube-attained-radius, lines 161-162, proved there from the imported Gaussian isoperimetric theorem of Borell and Sudakov-Tsirelson; nonzero law only).

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Wrappers SourceTubeAttained.tube_rayleigh_transfer_paper_l21 (nonzero law, only TubeTail supplied; TubeAttained discharged by tubeAttained_paperTube, wave L21) and SourceTube.tube_rayleigh_transfer_zero_paper (zero law, nothing supplied). Retained SourceTube.tube_rayleigh_transfer_paper, tube_rayleigh_transfer and measurable_tubeRadius take TubeAttained. Lower integrals in [0, infinity].

Proposition P:uniform-mean-regulator: Uniform approximation of the completed mean

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean constructs, with CutoffCompact supplied, under H:homog, Gamma != 0, 2 < r < 2/alpha0, L15's UniformMeanRegulator: T_R (R >= 1), C_t compact into L^r(I), C_t f = K f on tests, U with its tensor formula and ||U|| <= ||C_t||, and ||T_R U|| <= M_0 c_t uniformly in R >= 1; its mean has compact values a.e. The projections P_ret, Q_(J,K), eps_J -> 0 and the tail bound are not formalized.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves the mask family and every rate statement with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for lambda_(R,s) defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum of m_R h_s (compact ground rates not formalized); E:variational-unmasked-point-lower is derived from E:raw-block-original-lower as a supplied input, for a real function in place of the point moment.

In the paper. The statement is not quoted here; read it in the paper.

      (∀ R, R₀ ≤ R → IntegrableOn (maskedRate alpha0 Γ Ψ R) (Ioo 0 1)) ∧

      Tendsto (maskedIntegratedRate alpha0 Γ Ψ) atTop (𝓝 (integratedRate alpha0 Γ Ψ))) ∧

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: E:raw-block-original-lower of P:raw-block-original-lower for the masks m_R, all large R and one fixed x, with the compact ground rate of m_R h_s read as its Rayleigh rate and v_Psi as its integral form; used only by the point-moment display.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. The rate part states exactly the section's hypotheses (H:homog, Gamma != 0, a = alpha0) with nothing supplied: mask family, common margin, monotonicity in R, Lipschitz bound in s, exchange of suprema, pointwise and uniform convergence on [0,1], integral convergence. Only the point display uses the input; the solution u is not defined in Lean.

Hypotheses. The paper's own: the Lean statement assumes nothing the paper does not.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. Route: a finite-cell selection replaces the countable one, space-time Cauchy-Schwarz replaces rho_g in H_I. The class O itself in ClassOBridge (wave L14); the zero case Gamma = 0 is proved except C_2 = 0, the vanishing of S_c^pos and of the original means, and Q = 0 (ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper); the K_0 R_sp form (wave L8) remains. Le's decision of 2026-11-12 covered that L8 form.

Theorem T:white-moment-bounds: Explicit white moment bounds

Verified: a weaker statement. Lean accepts the proof, and lean-pkg's record shows every check that applies to this result passed (the build; its statement was not compared by a second checker).

Conclusion. A weaker statement than the paper's: Lean proves E:white-moment-bounds for the variational value S_2^pos in place of C_2(c,a) (identified by T:intrinsic-second-moment), for c > 0 and 0 < a < 1, with the value E_sp = c^2/6 of P:white-spatial-energy supplied (each bound uses one inequality of it), and that M_a, K_0(a) and both bound formulas are positive; the time exponent sentence and the case c = 0 are not formalized.

Hypotheses. The paper's, plus these, which the Lean statement assumes and the paper proves or assumes elsewhere: P:white-spatial-energy (integrated_white_evaluation.tex lines 79-133): the spatial energy of c delta_0 is c^2/6 for c > 0; the lower bound uses only c^2/6 <= E_sp (the sech profile, lines 106-124), the upper bound only E_sp <= c^2/6 (the CDF square, lines 88-100 and 117-121); reserved package B9, not proved.

Axioms. At most Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (what the build check records for the whole package).

Note. TeX route: the bracket of C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket (nothing supplied) at the white model (H:homog with alpha = d = 1, Gamma != 0 for c > 0, proved) and the arithmetic of lines 154-161. On the upper half also S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) <= the upper formula, via the exact C_occ (OccupationCeilingExact) over the class O modelled by joint representatives, not identified with the TeX's class.

Every result with each of its claims, in one table: Coverage.

Not formalized

  • Theorem T:full-upper (Full upper scale): main result; not formalized (the SPDE, stochastic integrals and analytic asymptotics are outside Lean)
  • Theorem T:intrinsic-second-moment (Intrinsic original second-moment constant): main result; not formalized (the SPDE, stochastic integrals and analytic asymptotics are outside Lean)

What the checks establish

  • Every proof is checked by Lean. The package builds; no sorry (an unfinished proof) remains; the only axioms used are Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext (allowed: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).
  • The statements shown are the ones proved. For 2056 statement(s), a second checker (comparator) confirmed that the proof proves exactly the statement shown, with only the permitted axioms, and independent Lean kernels replayed the proof.
  • Not checked by any tool: that a Lean statement says what the paper says. That is the comparison this page asks you to make. A definition listed under Definitions checked by a person is compared by name and type only.
